A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MM-Embed. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and can be matched despite renaming and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval and reranking experiments on M-BEIR, MTEB and CIRCO, together with ablations and qualitative case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, modality diagnostics and measured retrieval efficiency.

M1.justification: The architecture, contrastive training, two-type modality-aware negative mining, subsequent text-retrieval fine-tuning and True/False reranking procedure remain unchanged. NVEmb renames the existing NV-Embed-v1-based variant; the expanded negative-sampling explanation does not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same M-BEIR datasets and tasks, 15 MTEB retrieval datasets, CIRCO validation set and text-training corpora. Added comparisons and diagnostics reuse this coverage; the local-corpus comparisons change evaluation procedures rather than introduce new datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds BLIPFF to the M-BEIR comparison in Table 1 and CIRCO retrieval/reranking comparison in Table 4. E5-V and MagicLens, previously compared only on CIRCO, are additionally evaluated against MM-Embed on M-BEIR under global and local settings in Tables 12–13. This substantially broadens the relevant benchmark comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 introduces storage and latency evaluation using 100 sampled test queries per M-BEIR task and batch size 1. Table 13 adds local-corpus comparisons on selected subtasks. Existing training budgets, retrieval splits, accuracy metrics and top-10 reranking procedures are retained.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands the diagnostics: Table 14 extends modality-accuracy analysis beyond MSCOCO to all M-BEIR tasks, Table 11 examines training-modality frequencies as a possible explanation for retrieval bias, and Appendix A.2 profiles efficiency. Earlier instruction, training-strategy and reranking ablations and Figures 2–3 case studies remain.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports the 1st, 50th and 99th percentiles of query-encoding latency in Table 8. This describes variation across sampled queries, not uncertainty across repeated training runs. Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Substantial results are added while existing headline scores remain unchanged: MM-Embed still scores 52.7 on M-BEIR and 60.3 on MTEB. New entries include BLIPFF's 45.5 M-BEIR average, E5-V/MagicLens global averages of 11.5/5.8, random-negative models' MTEB results, wider modality accuracies and efficiency measurements. Table 8 reports an 86 GB MM-Embed index versus 16 GB for CLIPSF and BLIPFF.

T1.justification: The retrieval formulation and contrastive objective remain mathematically equivalent after matching notation and candidate sets. The discussion of the ideal full corpus, sampled negatives and batch-size matching expands the explanation; no new theorem, proof or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction drops v1's claim to be the first work exploring zero-shot MLLM reranking, instead emphasizing its application across multimodal tasks. The central claims about MM-Embed, modality-aware negative mining, text-retrieval preservation and benchmark performance remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds hypotheses connecting BLIP's domain performance to pretraining data, text-retrieval decline after hard-negative training to bias mitigation, and single-modal reranking failures to missing task/domain knowledge. It also argues against random sampling as the source of modality bias and explicitly discusses retrieval efficiency costs.

D1.justification: v2 supplies the BLIPFF checkpoint location and documents efficiency-measurement hardware, single-threaded execution, batch size and two-GPU index sharding. Existing training hyperparameters, image-token processing, training hardware and MM-Embed weight-access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a focused reranking discussion, including Ma et al., Zhuang et al., Qu et al. and Li et al., and distinguishes this work's multimodal queries from Qu's text-query setting. The conclusion adds Han et al. on iterative retrieval. The bibliography also loses the FEVER reference, replacing its citations with a duplicated counterargument-paper reference.

P1.justification: v2 copyedits the prose, standardizes NVEmb and continuous-fine-tuning terminology, and expands method explanations. References move before the reorganized appendix, while the main six-section narrative and most paragraph organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redrawn into separate retriever-training and frozen-reranking panels. Five appendix tables are added, existing comparison tables gain rows or columns, and several tables are resized or relocated. Figure 2 gains explicit negative-class labels; its examples and Figure 3's cases are retained.

improvement.justification: The added baseline comparisons, broader modality diagnostics and explicit storage/latency costs improve empirical support and transparency without changing the main results. Narrowing the reranking novelty claim also improves positioning. Small new errors, including the FEVER miscitation and stale Figure 1 task references, temper these useful but supplementary gains.
